chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When the one in Ihram complains (of illness), let him be treated with that which he eats, while he is in Ihram.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram
key_terms.يَتَدَاوَ: Let him be treated / seek medicine

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim in Ihram who falls ill and needs treatment?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a pilgrim in Ihram may treat illness by consuming ordinary food, provided it is not specifically prohibited for Ihram (like hunting or specific scents), thereby prioritizing health preservation within the ritual state. Scholars note this ruling prevents unnecessary hardship, aligning with the principle of *raf' al-haraj* (removal of difficulty), and distinguishes between general sustenance and specific medicinal substances that might carry their own rulings. It serves as a foundational text in Shia fiqh for balancing ritual purity with physical well-being during Hajj and Umrah.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the one in Ihraam complains, so let him be treated with that what he eats, while he is in Ihraam’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Isma‘il ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl from abu al-Sabbah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one in the state of Ihram becomes ill one must treat the illness with edible items while he is in the state of Ihram.”’
